trial_name: ROX TXA — Prehospital Tranexamic Acid in Traumatic Brain Injury (2020)
citation: Rowell SE, Meier EN, McKnight B, et al. Effect of out-of-hospital tranexamic acid vs placebo on 6-month functional neurologic outcomes in patients with moderate or severe traumatic brain injury. JAMA. 2020;324(10):961-974.
one_liner: Prehospital tranexamic acid did not significantly improve 6-month functional neurological outcome in non-hypotensive patients with suspected moderate-to-severe TBI.

pico.population: Out-of-hospital patients age >=15 years (or >50 kg) with suspected moderate-to-severe TBI (GCS <=12) without shock (SBP >=90 mmHg) treated within 2 hours of injury.
pico.intervention: Prehospital tranexamic acid (TXA) as either a 2 g bolus-only strategy or a 1 g bolus plus 1 g 8-hour in-hospital maintenance strategy.
pico.comparison: Matching placebo out-of-hospital infusion plus 8-hour in-hospital maintenance infusion.
pico.outcome: Favourable functional neurological outcome at 6 months, defined as Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE) >4.

background.existing_knowledge: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability with few proven pharmacological treatments. Early intracranial hemorrhage expansion and trauma-induced coagulopathy contribute to secondary brain injury.
background.knowledge_gap: Uncertainty remained regarding whether ultra-early prehospital TXA administration improves long-term functional outcomes in non-hypotensive TBI and which dosing regimen is optimal and safe.
background.hypothesis: Prehospital TXA improves 6-month functional neurological outcome in non-shock suspected moderate-to-severe TBI, with potential differences between 2 g bolus-only vs 1 g bolus plus 1 g maintenance infusion strategies.

methods.design: Randomised, multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm group sequential trial (Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium).
methods.setting: 12 ROC sites comprising 39 EMS agencies and 20 trauma centres in the US and Canada (conducted May 2015 to November 2017).

inclusion: Age >=15 years or estimated weight >50 kg
Blunt or penetrating trauma with suspected TBI
Prehospital GCS <=12 prior to sedatives or paralytics
At least 1 reactive pupil (or both reactive if GCS 4–12)
Ability to start out-of-hospital infusion within 2 hours of injury
exclusion: Time from injury to infusion >2 hours or unknown
Suspected seizure activity, acute MI, or stroke
Known history of seizures, thromboembolic disorder, or renal dialysis

methods.intervention: Bolus-maintenance strategy (1 g TXA in 250 mL prehospital + 1 g/8 h in-hospital) OR Bolus-only strategy (2 g TXA in 250 mL prehospital + placebo in-hospital over 8 h).
methods.comparison: Placebo 250 mL out-of-hospital infusion followed by placebo in-hospital infusion over 8 hours.
methods.blinding: Double-blind (prehospital clinicians, in-hospital clinicians, patients, outcome assessors).
methods.sample_size_power: 1200 planned to yield ~963 treated patients for analysis; designed to detect a 7% absolute difference in favourable outcome (combined TXA vs placebo) with 80% power using asymmetric group sequential design (1-sided alpha=0.10 for benefit, 1-sided alpha=0.025 for harm).
methods.primary_outcome: Favourable functional neurological outcome at 6 months (GOSE >4).
secondary_outcomes: Progression of intracranial haemorrhage at 24 hours (>33% increase in volume on paired CT)
methods.follow_up: 28 days for mortality/early clinical events; 6 months for GOSE and DRS.

headline_bullets: Favourable 6-month functional outcome did not differ significantly between combined TXA strategies and placebo (65% vs 62%; adjusted difference 3.5%, 95% CI -0.9 to 10.2).
Overall 28-day mortality was 14% with TXA vs 17% with placebo (adjusted difference -2.9%, 95% CI -7.9 to 2.1).
Seizures occurred more frequently with 2 g bolus TXA (5% vs 2% placebo), while thromboembolic events were lower with bolus-maintenance TXA (4% vs 10% placebo).
An exploratory subgroup with CT-confirmed intracranial hemorrhage showed reduced 28-day mortality with the 2 g bolus strategy (18% vs 27%, p=0.03).

outcomes_table.note: Combined TXA vs placebo; site-adjusted; primary endpoint; missing GOSE imputed
Combined TXA vs placebo; 87% of deaths attributed to neurological injury
Combined TXA vs placebo; lower scores indicate less disability

outcomes_table.outcome: Progression of intracranial haemorrhage at 24 hours
outcomes_table.note: Combined TXA vs placebo; paired CT required; defined as >33% volume increase
Bolus-only TXA vs placebo; bolus-only vs bolus-maintenance difference 3.4% (95% CI 0.7 to 6.1)
Bolus-maintenance TXA vs placebo; composite vascular occlusive outcome

subgroup_table.subgroup: 28-day mortality with intracranial haemorrhage on initial CT

safety: Seizure/seizure-like activity occurred in 17/345 (5%) of bolus-only TXA vs 7/309 (2%) of placebo (adjusted diff 2.8%, 95% CI -0.1 to 5.6; difference between bolus-only and bolus-maintenance was 3.4%, 95% CI 0.7 to 6.1).
Thromboembolic events occurred in 13/312 (4%) of bolus-maintenance TXA vs 30/309 (10%) of placebo (adjusted diff -5.8%, 95% CI -9.8 to -1.8).
Divergent safety profiles between 2 g bolus-only and bolus-maintenance regimens indicate dose- and administration-dependent effects.

domains.notes: Computer-generated randomisation using permuted blocks (sizes 3 and 6); allocation concealed via sequentially used identical study kits on EMS vehicles.
Double-blinded with matched placebo kits. Emergency unblinding was rare (7/312, 4/345, 11/309), with open-label TXA given in 53% of unblinded cases.
1063 randomised; 97 did not receive infusion and 1 incarcerated patient was excluded, leaving 966 treated patients for modified ITT analysis.
Prehospital infusion completion was 93–95%; in-hospital infusion was initiated in 79–86% and completed in 69–77% of patients.

Groups well balanced except penetrating mechanism (4% bolus-maintenance, 1% bolus-only, 5% placebo). Median time from injury to start of prehospital infusion was ~40 min (43 min, 40 min, 41 min across arms).

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is moderate: strong randomisation, concealment, and ultra-early delivery, but post-randomisation exclusions (97 untreated) and incomplete in-hospital infusions reduce precision.

domains.notes: Applies to non-hypotensive (SBP >=90 mmHg) suspected TBI treated within 2 hours in advanced EMS systems. Excludes hypotensive, polytrauma, delayed (>2h), or pediatric (<15 yrs) patients.
Pragmatic prehospital enrolment led to ~20% of patients having in-hospital GCS >12 and ~24% having no head injury on AIS, diluting potential TBI-specific treatment effect.

external_validity.verdict: External validity is moderate: generalisable to early prehospital management of non-hypotensive suspected TBI in high-resource EMS systems, but not to hypotensive hemorrhagic trauma.

strengths: Large, multicentre, double-blind prehospital RCT evaluating patient-centred 6-month functional outcomes
Ultra-early drug administration with median time to infusion start of ~40 minutes from injury
Rigorous evaluation of two distinct dosing regimens (2 g bolus vs 1 g + 1 g maintenance)
limitations: Modified ITT analysis excluded 97 randomised but untreated patients post-randomisation
Incomplete in-hospital infusion completion (69–77%) reduced separation between TXA strategies
Missing 6-month outcome data required multiple imputation (20 datasets)
Primary analysis combined two divergent TXA regimens
Excluded patients with shock or polytrauma

critical_appraisal.summary: A high-quality, prehospital double-blind RCT demonstrating that hyperacute TXA does not significantly improve 6-month functional outcome in non-hypotensive suspected TBI.
strengths: Double-blind design with identical study kits
weaknesses: Pragmatic field enrollment resulted in ~24% of patients without head injury
Primary endpoint combined two regimens with divergent safety and mortality trends

sections.authors_conclusion: Out-of-hospital TXA administration did not significantly improve 6-month functional outcome in patients with moderate-to-severe TBI who were not in shock.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Routine prehospital TXA should not be administered purely for neuroprotection in hemodynamically stable suspected TBI.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Prehospital adult and adolescent trauma patients with suspected moderate-to-severe TBI (GCS <=12) and SBP >=90 mmHg.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Does not refute the efficacy of TXA in traumatic hemorrhagic shock or bleeding trauma.
implementation_caveats: 2 g bolus-only TXA strategy increased seizure activity (5% vs 2% placebo).
Pragmatic prehospital criteria capture a heterogeneous population with high rates (~24%) of minor or non-head injuries.

controversies.notes: Field criteria enrolled ~20% of patients with in-hospital GCS >12 and ~24% with no head injury on AIS, potentially diluting treatment effects.

Bolus-only 2 g TXA increased seizure risk (5% vs 2%), whereas bolus-maintenance showed lower thromboembolic rates (4% vs 10%). Mortality reduction in CT-positive patients was limited to the 2 g bolus strategy (18% vs 27%, p=0.03).
A correction amended a TEG clot lysis table value (>3% lysis at 30 min) from 31 to 3 in the bolus-only group, reflecting data curation challenges without altering primary findings.

CRASH-3 found no overall head-injury mortality benefit (RR 0.94; 95% CI 0.86 to 1.02), while meta-analyses show reduced haematoma expansion (RR 0.77; 95% CI 0.63 to 0.93) without improved functional outcome.

context_related_trials.relation: In-hospital trial showing no overall reduction in head-injury mortality with TXA (RR 0.94; 95% CI 0.86 to 1.02), aligned with ROC TXA neutral functional results.

Observational prehospital study showing no overall 30-day mortality benefit with TXA (OR 1.17; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.65) and higher adjusted mortality in isolated severe TBI (OR 2.05; 95% CI 1.22 to 3.45).

unresolved_questions: Does ultra-early TXA benefit specific neuroimaging-confirmed TBI subgroups (e.g., CT-positive intracranial hemorrhage)?
What is the optimal TXA dose that balances reduction in hematoma expansion against seizure activity?
Can prehospital biomarker enrichment refine candidate selection for acute TBI therapies?

numbers_to_remember: Primary GOSE >4 at 6 months: 65% TXA vs 62% Placebo (p=0.16)
Seizure activity: 5% (2 g bolus TXA) vs 2% (Placebo)
Median time to infusion start: ~40 minutes from injury
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: Prehospital TXA does not improve 6-month functional outcomes in non-hypotensive moderate-to-severe TBI and should not be routinely given solely for TBI neuroprotection.
